definition: What it represents is a comparison between two steady values of a quantity Q: its previous steady value, A, and its new set value, B. Their difference, B − A, is the gap the whole rest of the chain has to close — its size says how far Q has to travel, and its sign says which way: up if B > A, down if B < A. Nothing has changed yet at this step; the difference operator only measures the change that has been asked for.
name: Difference operator

definition: What it represents is two signals combined into one by adding them: the pair of the difference operator, for the places where a signal is genuinely the sum of two parts. Its place in this note is the system diagram, where a signal's position part — the value of Q at a point, constant at that point — adds with its time part, Q(t), an oscillator. Because the position part is constant, the output of the adding is an oscillator that just becomes Q(t) again: adding a constant to the oscillator does not change its kind. Adding is this operator; multiplying is the mixer, ⊗; subtracting is the difference operator.
name: Addition operator — the adder, ⊕

definition: What it represents is a component: a heat source, like the terrarium's heating pad. It generates an environmental signal — a temperature signal, or a heat signal, depending on which quantity we track. The signal is not drawn as a block in a diagram; it is what is measured on the lines leaving the component. Its temperature T settles from its previous value T_o toward the set value T_s that drives it, closing at a rate proportional to the gap that remains. The differential equation is Newton's law of cooling, dT/dt = −k(T − T_s) — first-order linear, solved by separation of variables — and its solution is T(t) = T_s + (T_o − T_s)·e^(−kt), where k is Boltzmann's constant, a fixed constant of the model. Function type of the solution: exponential. Whether it climbs or falls is set by the sign of T_s − T_o: heating and cooling are the same signal, closing the gap from opposite sides.
name: Heat Source

definition: What it represents is one signal scaling another by multiplication: a transform carried out as a product. In this note the mixer is where the signal meets position: the exponential Q(t) runs through a transform that depends on the point, so the value of Q at point b is its value at point a reduced by the factor the move from a to b imposes — what comes out is the same signal, reduced by exactly that factor. The mixer does not add anything of its own; it applies one input to the other. (Addition is a different operation — the adder, ⊕, defined beside the difference operator above.)
name: Mixer — ⊗
Thermostat
definition: What it represents is a component: the thermostat. It generates a control signal — the set temperature T_s, dialled in and held constant. The signal is not drawn as a block in a diagram; it is what is measured on the line leaving the thermostat, and everything else in the system chases it. Turn the dial and T_s takes a new value; between turns, it is constant. Function type: constant. It is drawn with a gear around the outside and a dial inside, so control components can be told apart at a glance.

What it represents is a component: a filter. It generates a transform — temperature falling off with distance: a temperature that is constant in time at every point, but whose value falls exponentially as position x grows — the attenuation of heat as it travels through a medium. The signal it generates is the attenuation itself: α(x) = e^(−cx), the factor a temperature signal is reduced by after travelling the distance x. Its value at position x is set by three numbers: the temperature at x = 0, the end temperature it falls toward as x grows, and the cutoff rate, which sets how fast the fall happens — a large cutoff rate spends the heat quickly, a small one lets it reach far. The equation along x, dT/dx = −c(T − T_end), is first-order linear, and its solution is an exponential in position rather than in time, so nothing in it ever changes with time.
name: Thermodynamic filter
